lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What if every promise you heard... left a thread?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A real one. Glowing. Tied from their wrist... to your heart.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Keep the promise, and it lights up like a firework. Break it...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ...and it hangs there. Grey. For everyone to see. Well. For YOU to see.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wake up. Your alarm promises, "five more minutes."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The thread snaps grey before you even sit up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Downstairs, Mom says, "I'll drive you today." Gold. Thick. Already glowing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your little brother promises he'll "clean his room THIS time."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His wrist... is a mess.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The rules are simple. Every promise makes a thread. Big promises, thick threads. Kept ones turn to light. Broken ones turn grey... and drag.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bus driver: "I'll wait for you!"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A billboard promises "your best summer ever." The thread goes up into the sky, and just... ends.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By lunch, you learn the first secret. Most promises aren't lies. People just... forget.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At school, it's like seeing the future.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: "I'll pay you back Friday." Thin. Already sagging. You keep your money.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ms. Bell: "I'll grade them by Monday." Twenty-eight threads, one to every desk, all still gold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She means it. She's just tired.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At casino night, a kid swears he'll "split the winnings." The thread is already grey before the cards are dealt.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You stop trusting words. You start trusting threads.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Group projects? You pick the gold ones. Dates? Gold ones. Friends?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For about a week, your life is perfectly organised... by light.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then you notice Maya.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There's a thread between you. Old. From a long time ago.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: "I'll always save you a seat." You remember her saying it. In second grade.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's still there. Still gold. Barely. Because she still saves it. Every day. And you never sit there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You start seeing it everywhere. Not lies. Just... waiting.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Late at night, you find Dad at the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He has one thread. One. Thick as a rope. Gold. Going to every one of you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You ask him what he promised. He laughs. "That I'd take care of you."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He never said it out loud. Not once. And it's the brightest thread in the house.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night, you can't sleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go to the bathroom, turn on the light... and look in the mirror.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You never thought to look at your OWN wrist.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There are hundreds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: "I'll start tomorrow." "I'll call Grandma." "I'll be nicer to Leo." "I'll text you back."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most of them are grey. And they all lead... to people you love.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But one is older than all the others.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You follow it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It leads to YOU. Seven years old.

lines.speaker: kid
lines.text: I'll be brave.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Promises to yourself count too. You just never see them break.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the next morning, you keep one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Just one. Small.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You sit in the seat Maya saves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the thread between you... doesn't snap.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It ignites.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You call Grandma. Gold. You help Leo clean his room. He's so shocked, HIS thread bursts too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your wrist doesn't get lighter overnight. But it gets brighter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And that oldest thread? You're working on it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So. If you could see every promise you've made...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ...how many would still be waiting?
